# **1\. Introduction**

## **1.1 Purpose**

This System Design Document (SDD) defines the technical architecture, database schema, API design, and user interface flows for the Vendor Performance Intelligence Platform. It is derived from the requirements defined in URD-PERSONAL-002 and serves as the primary technical reference for implementation.

## **1.2 Scope**

The system covers two modules built on a shared data entry layer: Module 1 (Recurring Vendor Performance Reports) and Module 2 (Vendor Scorecard Dashboard). Vendor and transaction data management is shared infrastructure underlying both.

In scope:

*   Bulk file upload or manual single-entry of vendor and transaction records
*   Computation of quantitative performance metrics across three benchmarks: delivery timing, pricing consistency, and order accuracy
*   Periodic generation of AI-assisted vendor performance reports
*   A continuously available dashboard summarising all-time vendor performance

Out of scope:

*   Bid comparison or competing-vendor evaluation
*   Multi-user access control or department-based data segregation
*   Evaluation of vendor quality of goods/services or vendor responsiveness
*   Integration with external procurement, ERP, or accounting systems

## **1.3 Design Principles**

*   Deterministic-first, AI-narrated-second — all quantitative metrics are computed by application logic; the AI model explains, never calculates, and its output is validated against source data before being shown
*   Traceability by design — every performance judgement, whether a number or a sentence, must be traceable to recorded transaction data
*   Free-tier bounded — all architecture and service tier choices operate within the free-tier limits of Azure, Vercel, and Google Gemini
*   Single-tenant, single-user — the platform uses its own dedicated Azure tenant and database, independent of any other system; no requirement assumes concurrent multi-user access
*   Defense-in-depth for immutability — critical invariants (Finalized report immutability, referenced-vendor deletion protection) are enforced at both the application layer and the database layer
*   NULL means no data, zero means measured zero — this distinction is preserved throughout the schema and all computation logic

# **2\. System Architecture**

## **2.1 Architecture Overview**

The system follows a three-tier architecture: a Next.js frontend/backend (App Router), Google Gemini as the AI narrative provider, and an Azure SQL Database. The application is hosted on Vercel; authentication, database, secrets, and AI provider credentials are managed on Microsoft Azure. This split-platform arrangement reflects the platform being Vercel-hosted for the application layer while Azure remains the system of record for identity, data, and secrets, per the URD's dedicated-tenant constraint.

All backend logic is implemented as Next.js API Routes rather than Server Actions, so that each operation can be tested independently of the UI (e.g., via Postman or automated tests) and documented as an explicit request/response contract.

| **Layer** | **Technology** |
| --- | --- |
| Client Layer | Single user, web browser (desktop/tablet) |
| Auth Layer | Microsoft Entra ID (MSAL) — sign-in and session |
| App Layer | Next.js (App Router) — hosted on Vercel; API Routes handle Gemini calls, metric computation, PDF/Word export |
| Data Layer | Azure SQL Database (serverless, free offer tier) |
| Platform | Azure Key Vault (secrets, via Service Principal from Vercel), Google Gemini API |

## **2.2 Component Breakdown**

| **Component** | **Technology** | **Responsibility** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Next.js App | Next.js 14+ (App Router), Tailwind CSS | Vendor/transaction entry UI, report generation UI, dashboard, all client-facing rendering |
| API Routes | Next.js API Routes | CRUD for vendors/transactions, metric computation trigger, Gemini invocation, PDF/Word generation, bulk upload validation |
| Metric Engine | Application logic (TypeScript, within API routes) | Deterministic computation of all 9 metrics; never delegated to AI |
| AI Narrative Service | Google Gemini API (server-side call only) | Generates narrative from structured metric input; every numeric value in the output is extracted and checked against the supplied data before display — narrative containing an unmatched number is rejected and regeneration is attempted |
| Document Export | Server-side document-generation library (no headless browser) | Produces the Finalized report as both PDF and Word (.docx), generated entirely server-side from stored content |
| Database | Azure SQL Database (serverless) | All relational data: vendors, transactions, reports, metrics |
| Secrets | Azure Key Vault, accessed via Service Principal | AI API key, DB connection string — retrieved at startup, cached in memory |

## **2.3 Azure Resource Topology**

Unlike a single-cloud deployment, this system's resources span two platforms. Azure resources are provisioned within a single Resource Group; the application itself is deployed separately on Vercel and connects to Azure resources over the public internet with firewall-restricted access (see Section 7, Security Design).

| **Resource** | **Tier / Plan** | **Notes** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vercel | Free (Hobby) tier | Hosts Next.js app; serverless function execution; no idle-sleep penalty affecting AI generation |
| Azure SQL Database | Serverless, General Purpose, Free Offer | 100,000 vCore-seconds + 32 GB storage free/month; auto-pauses when idle |
| Azure Key Vault | Standard | Stores AI API key, DB connection string; accessed via Service Principal |
| Azure Entra ID | Free tier (App Registration) | Authentication provider (MSAL) |
| Google Gemini API | Free tier | If the provider returns a rate-limit error, the system retries with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s delays), up to 3 attempts; if all attempts fail, the user is told AI generation is temporarily unavailable rather than the system continuing to retry |

## **2.4 Authentication Flow**

The platform has a single authentication flow: internal sign-in via Microsoft Entra ID. There is no external/client-facing authentication path, since this platform has no external client-facing module.

Users authenticate via Entra ID using MSAL.js in the Next.js frontend, following the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Flow with PKCE. Upon successful login, an access token is attached as a Bearer token to API requests. The API layer validates the token against Entra ID's JWKS endpoint.

Separately, at application startup, the Next.js server authenticates to Azure Key Vault using a Service Principal (client ID + client secret stored as Vercel environment variables) to retrieve the database connection string and Gemini API key, which are cached in memory for the lifetime of the running instance, rather than being stored as plaintext environment variables or re-fetched on every request.

# **3\. Database Design**

## **3.1 Overview**

The database is Azure SQL Database, serverless General Purpose tier. The schema is organised around three domains: Vendor & Transaction Data, Reporting, and Metrics. All tables use int IDENTITY(1,1) primary keys. No soft-delete pattern is used — the schema instead prevents deletion of referenced records outright.

_Naming convention: snake\_case for all tables and columns, UPPER\_SNAKE\_CASE for table names. All tables include a created\_at column defaulting to GETUTCDATE(). Foreign keys are enforced at the database level._

## **3.2 Entity Relationship Summary**

| **Domain** | **Tables** |
| --- | --- |
| Vendor & Transaction Data | VENDORS, VENDOR\_TRANSACTIONS |
| Reporting | VENDOR\_PERFORMANCE\_REPORTS, VENDOR\_PERFORMANCE\_REPORT\_VENDORS |
| Metrics | VENDOR\_PERFORMANCE\_METRICS |

## **3.3 Core Table Schemas**

**3.3.1 VENDORS**

| **Column** | **Type** | **Constraints** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| id | int | PK, IDENTITY(1,1) | Unique vendor identifier |
| name | nvarchar(200) | NOT NULL | Vendor name |
| registration\_number | nvarchar(50) | UNIQUE, NOT NULL | Business registration number |
| contact\_info | nvarchar(500) | NOT NULL | Contact details |
| created\_at | datetime2 | NOT NULL, DEFAULT GETUTCDATE() | Record creation timestamp |

**3.3.2 VENDOR\_TRANSACTIONS**

| **Column** | **Type** | **Constraints** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| id | int | PK, IDENTITY(1,1) | Unique transaction identifier |
| vendor\_id | int | FK → VENDORS, ON DELETE RESTRICT | Parent vendor |
| transaction\_date | date | NOT NULL, range 2000-01-01 to current date | Date of transaction |
| item\_description | nvarchar(500) | NOT NULL, max 500 chars | Item/service description |
| agreed\_price | decimal(12,2) | NOT NULL, > 0 | Agreed price |
| actual\_price | decimal(12,2) | NULL until delivery/invoice recorded, if present > 0 | Actual price charged |
| agreed\_delivery\_date | date | NOT NULL, ≥ transaction\_date | Promised delivery date |
| actual\_delivery\_date | date | NULL until delivery occurs, if present ≥ transaction\_date | Actual delivery date |
| quantity\_ordered | decimal(10,2) | NOT NULL, > 0 | Quantity ordered |
| quantity\_received | decimal(10,2) | NULL until delivery occurs, if present > 0 | Quantity actually received |
| created\_at | datetime2 | NOT NULL, DEFAULT GETUTCDATE() | Record creation timestamp |

**3.3.3 VENDOR\_PERFORMANCE\_REPORTS**

| **Column** | **Type** | **Constraints** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| id | int | PK, IDENTITY(1,1) | Unique report identifier |
| reference\_number | nvarchar(30) | NOT NULL | Human-readable reference |
| period\_type | nvarchar(20) | NOT NULL, 'Quarterly' or 'Custom' | Report period type |
| period\_start | date | NOT NULL | Report period start |
| period\_end | date | NOT NULL, ≥ period\_start | Report period end |
| status | nvarchar(20) | NOT NULL, 'Draft'/'Finalized', default 'Draft' | Report status |
| vendor\_summary | nvarchar(MAX) | NULL | Report section content |
| delivery\_performance | nvarchar(MAX) | NULL | Report section content |
| pricing\_analysis | nvarchar(MAX) | NULL | Report section content |
| order\_accuracy | nvarchar(MAX) | NULL | Report section content |
| created\_at | datetime2 | NOT NULL, DEFAULT GETUTCDATE() | Record creation timestamp |
| finalized\_at | datetime2 | NULL | Timestamp when finalized |

**3.3.4 VENDOR\_PERFORMANCE\_REPORT\_VENDORS**

Linking table associating reports with the vendors included in them.

| **Column** | **Type** | **Constraints** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| report\_id | int | FK → VENDOR\_PERFORMANCE\_REPORTS | Parent report |
| vendor\_id | int | FK → VENDORS | Included vendor |

**3.3.5 VENDOR\_PERFORMANCE\_METRICS**

Stores computed metrics per vendor per period. Populated both when a report is generated and, for dashboard purposes, as an all-time aggregate per vendor (in which case report\_id is NULL).

| **Column** | **Type** | **Constraints** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| id | int | PK, IDENTITY(1,1) | Unique identifier |
| report\_id | int | FK, NULL for dashboard aggregation. Part of composite unique constraint. | Owning report, if any |
| vendor\_id | int | FK → VENDORS. Part of composite unique constraint. | Vendor this row measures |
| period\_start | date | NOT NULL. Part of composite unique constraint. | Period covered |
| period\_end | date | NOT NULL | Period covered |
| on\_time\_delivery\_rate | decimal(5,2) | NULL if no completed deliveries; else 0–100 | On-time delivery rate |
| avg\_delay\_days | decimal(6,2) | NULL if no completed deliveries; 0 if none late | Average delay in days |
| overcharge\_rate | decimal(5,2) | NULL if no priced transactions; else 0–100 | Overcharge rate |
| avg\_overcharge\_pct | decimal(6,2) | NULL if no priced transactions; 0 if none overcharged | Average overcharge % |
| undercharge\_rate | decimal(5,2) | NULL if no priced transactions; else 0–100 | Undercharge rate |
| shortfall\_rate | decimal(5,2) | NULL if no recorded quantity; else 0–100 | Shortfall rate |
| avg\_shortfall\_units | decimal(10,2) | NULL if no recorded quantity; 0 if none fell short | Average shortfall (units) |
| overdelivery\_rate | decimal(5,2) | NULL if no recorded quantity; else 0–100 | Over-delivery rate |
| avg\_overdelivery\_units | decimal(10,2) | NULL if no recorded quantity; 0 if none over-delivered | Average over-delivery (units) |
| transaction\_count | int | NOT NULL | Number of transactions in period |

## **3.4 Enforcement Mechanisms**

Composite uniqueness. A composite unique constraint on (report\_id, vendor\_id, period\_start) in VENDOR\_PERFORMANCE\_METRICS is enforced at the database level, preventing duplicate metric rows if a report generation process runs more than once for the same vendor and period.

Finalized report immutability. Enforced at two layers: the application layer rejects edit/delete requests against a report with status = 'Finalized' before they reach the database; a database trigger on VENDOR\_PERFORMANCE\_REPORTS independently blocks any UPDATE or DELETE where status = 'Finalized', regardless of the source of the operation. The trigger is the authoritative enforcement — the application check exists only to give faster feedback to the user.

Referenced-record protection. VENDOR\_TRANSACTIONS.vendor\_id uses ON DELETE RESTRICT, preventing deletion of a vendor referenced by any transaction. A transaction referenced by a Finalized report is similarly protected at the application layer, which checks for that reference before permitting an edit or delete and, if found, rejects the action with a message naming the report.

# **4\. API Design**

## **4.1 API Conventions**

*   All requests and responses use JSON (Content-Type: application/json)
*   All routes require a valid Entra ID Bearer token in the Authorization header — there is no unauthenticated route on this platform
*   Dates: ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD); timestamps: UTC ISO 8601 with timezone
*   Errors return a consistent shape: { error: string, field?: string, row?: number } — the field/row keys are populated for validation errors so a bulk upload failure identifies exactly which row and column caused it

## **4.2 Vendors & Transactions (Shared Data Layer)**

| **Method** | **Endpoint** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | /api/vendors | List all vendor records |
| POST | /api/vendors | Create a new vendor record; before creation, the entered name is compared against existing vendor names using a string-similarity method, and if the similarity score is 85% or higher, the match is returned for user confirmation instead of creating the record immediately |
| DELETE | /api/vendors/:id | Delete a vendor record; rejected if the vendor is referenced by any transaction or report |
| GET | /api/transactions | List transaction records, filterable by vendor and date range |
| POST | /api/transactions | Create a transaction record via manual single-entry |
| PUT | /api/transactions/:id | Edit a transaction record; rejected if referenced by a Finalized report, with a message naming the report |
| DELETE | /api/transactions/:id | Delete a transaction record; same Finalized-report rejection rule as edit |
| POST | /api/transactions/bulk-upload | Upload a CSV/Excel file of transactions; missing required columns reject the whole file; rows with invalid data, dates, or out-of-range values are skipped and reported by row number and reason, while valid rows are still saved |

## **4.3 Module 1 — Recurring Vendor Performance Reports**

| **Method** | **Endpoint** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | /api/reports | List all reports (Draft and Finalized), supporting period-over-period comparison |
| POST | /api/reports | Create a new report for a Quarterly (default) or Custom date range; vendors to include are selected before generation |
| GET | /api/reports/:id | Get full report content including all four section fields and computed metrics |
| POST | /api/reports/:id/generate | Trigger metric computation and AI narrative generation for the selected vendors and period, computing nine metrics for the current period, prior period, and peer average; rejected with a message if generation is already in progress for this report |
| PUT | /api/reports/:id | Edit report section content while in Draft status |
| POST | /api/reports/:id/finalize | Transition a report to Finalized status; rejected if any of the four section fields remain empty |
| DELETE | /api/reports/:id | Delete a report; only permitted while in Draft status |
| GET | /api/reports/:id/export?format=pdf&#124;docx | Export a Finalized report as PDF or Word, generated server-side from stored content |

## **4.4 Module 2 — Vendor Scorecard Dashboard**

| **Method** | **Endpoint** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | /api/dashboard | List all vendors with at least one recorded transaction and their all-time metrics; sortable by any metric column, with insufficient-data vendors grouped separately at the end |
| GET | /api/dashboard?threshold=:n | Same as above, but any metric with fewer valid transactions than the given threshold is shown as insufficient data rather than a calculated value |
| GET | /api/dashboard/vendors/:id | Get a vendor's complete transaction history for the detail drill-down view |

# **5\. UI/UX Screen Flows**

## **5.1 Design System**

*   Component framework: Next.js (App Router) with Tailwind CSS
*   Design language: Clean, data-dense where needed (metric tables, dashboard), minimal chrome elsewhere
*   Form validation: Inline, real-time — errors shown at the specific field, and for bulk upload, at the specific row
*   Responsive breakpoints: Desktop-primary — this is an internal single-user tool with no field/mobile use case

## **5.2 Screen Inventory**

| **Screen** | **Key Elements** | **Actions / Transitions** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vendor List | Table of all vendors, search bar, Add Vendor button | Open vendor → Vendor Detail; Add Vendor → creation form |
| Vendor Detail | Vendor info, linked transaction history | Edit vendor info; navigate to filtered Transaction List |
| Transaction List | Table of transactions, filter by vendor/date, Add/Bulk Upload buttons | Open transaction → edit (if unlocked); Bulk Upload → upload flow |
| Bulk Upload | File picker, upload button, post-upload result summary | Upload → validation → result summary shown inline |
| Report List | Table of Draft and Finalized reports, New Report button | Open report → Report Editor; New Report → creation flow |
| New Report | Period selector (Quarterly default/Custom), vendor multi-select | Generate → triggers computation + AI narrative, opens Report Editor |
| Report Editor | Four editable sections, computed metrics displayed, Finalize/Export buttons | Edit sections; Finalize → locks report; Export → PDF/Word download |
| Scorecard Dashboard | Sortable table of all-time metrics, insufficient-data threshold control | Sort by column; click vendor → Vendor Detail drill-down |

## **5.3 Key User Journey — Generating a Quarterly Report**

| **Step** | **Screen** | **What Happens** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Report List | User clicks New Report |
| 2 | New Report | Selects Quarterly period (default) and chooses which vendors to include |
| 3 | New Report → Report Editor | Clicks Generate; system computes all nine metrics per vendor for current period, prior period, and peer average, then sends structured data to the AI model |
| 4 | Report Editor | Generated narrative appears as an editable Draft; user reviews and edits any section |
| 5 | Report Editor | User clicks Finalize; system checks all four sections are non-empty before allowing the transition |
| 6 | Report Editor | User clicks Export, selects PDF or Word; file is generated server-side and downloaded |

# **6\. Data Flow Diagrams**

## **6.1 Level 0 — System Context**

At the highest level, the platform sits between the User (the single individual performing all three roles), Microsoft Entra ID (identity provider), and Google Gemini (AI narrative provider). The system mediates all data flow between them.

| **Actor** | **Data INTO the System** | **Data OUT of the System** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| User | Vendor records, transaction entries (manual or bulk), report generation requests, section edits, finalize/export actions | Vendor and transaction lists, computed metrics, report drafts, dashboard views, exported files, validation errors |
| Microsoft Entra ID | User identity token, session claims | Authentication confirmation |
| Google Gemini API | Structured metric data (current period, prior period, peer average) | Generated narrative text |

## **6.2 Level 1 — Core Processes**

| **Process** | **Input** | **Output** | **Data Store / Destination** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P1: Authenticate User | Entra ID token | Validated session with claims | No persistent storage — validated in memory against Entra ID's JWKS endpoint |
| P2: Manage Vendors & Transactions | Manual entry or bulk file upload | Vendor/transaction records; per-row result for bulk upload | DB: VENDORS, VENDOR\_TRANSACTIONS |
| P3: Compute Metrics | Transactions within selected report period and vendor set | Nine metrics per vendor for current, prior, and peer average; NULL where no eligible transactions | DB: VENDOR\_PERFORMANCE\_METRICS |
| P4: Generate Narrative | Structured metric data object | AI-generated narrative text | Held in memory pending validation — not yet saved |
| P5: Validate Narrative | Generated narrative, source metric data | Validated narrative, or rejection triggering regeneration | DB: VENDOR\_PERFORMANCE\_REPORTS (only on success) |
| P6: Finalize Report | Finalize action, four section fields | Updated report status; rejected if any section empty | DB: VENDOR\_PERFORMANCE\_REPORTS (status update) |
| P7: Export Report | Finalized report content | PDF or Word file, generated server-side | Delivered directly to user; not persisted separately |
| P8: Aggregate Dashboard Metrics | All-time transactions per vendor | All-time metrics per vendor, insufficient-data flags per metric | DB: VENDOR\_PERFORMANCE\_METRICS (report\_id NULL rows) |

# **7\. Security Design**

## **7.1 Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)**

All three roles defined in the URD — Procurement Staff, Report Reviewer, System Administrator — are currently performed by a single individual, so no role-gating is enforced at the application or API level. The table below documents which functions correspond to each role conceptually.

| **Permission** | **Procurement Staff** | **Report Reviewer** | **System Administrator** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Create/edit vendors and transactions | ✓ | — | — |
| Resolve ambiguous vendor matches | — | — | ✓ |
| Generate reports | — | ✓ | — |
| Edit Draft report sections | — | ✓ | — |
| Finalize reports | — | ✓ | — |
| View dashboard | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Manage system configuration | — | — | ✓ |

## **7.2 Data Security**

*   All data in transit is encrypted via HTTPS/TLS, standard for both Vercel and Azure SQL connections
*   All database queries use parameterized statements — no raw string concatenation into SQL
*   Displayed text relies on the frontend framework's default escaping; raw HTML is never rendered from user input
*   Exported PDF/Word content uses the export library's safe text-insertion method, not direct string concatenation
*   The AI API key and database connection string are stored in Azure Key Vault, retrieved at startup via a Service Principal, and cached in memory — never stored as plaintext environment variables and never re-fetched on every request
*   Because the application is hosted on Vercel rather than within Azure's network, Azure SQL Database's firewall is configured to accept connections only from Vercel's outbound IP ranges, rather than being open to the general internet

## **7.3 Application-Level Safeguards**

*   Finalized reports are immutable and non-deletable, enforced at both the application layer and the database layer (trigger)
*   Vendor records referenced by any transaction or report cannot be deleted; transactions referenced by a Finalized report cannot be edited or deleted
*   All quantitative metrics shown to the user are computed by deterministic application logic; the AI model's narrative is checked by extracting every numeric value and confirming each matches the supplied metric data, with unmatched values triggering rejection and regeneration
*   If a Draft report save fails due to an expired authentication session, the report's editable text fields are temporarily retained in browser session storage and restored after re-authentication; authentication tokens or credentials are never included
*   Duplicate or rapid repeated AI generation requests for the same report are prevented by checking whether a generation is already in progress before starting a new one
*   If the AI provider returns a rate-limit error, the request is retried with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s) up to 3 attempts; if all attempts fail, the user is told AI generation is temporarily unavailable

## **7.4 Cost & Resource Boundaries**

The application operates entirely within the free-tier limits of Vercel, Azure SQL Database, Azure Key Vault, and the Google Gemini API. No component of the architecture requires a paid tier under expected personal-project usage.
